newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Q2 current account moves to surplus.
newsitem.headline: Canada Q2 current account moves to surplus.

text.p: Canada's current account moved to a C$1.15 billion second quarter surplus seasonally adjusted from a C$1.62 billion (revised from C$1.94 billion) deficit in the first quarter, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
Note - Figures are in billions of Canadian dollars on a seasonally adjusted basis.

The revision in the first quarter current account deficit was due primarily due to an upward revision in the merchandise trade surplus to C$7.92 billion from C$7.00 billion, the agency's figures show.
The current account surplus was the first since the fourth quarter of 1984.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast a current account surplus of C$500 million in the quarter.
